beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent. You can share context, a skill, the output, or an interface.
beats.got: Sharing my setup means handing over four specific things, not the agent itself. That is exactly my problem with the fourteen private experiments.

beats.trigger: Walk in with one example where people had access to a tool or process but real use did not follow.
beats.got: I'll use our dispatch-board rollout last year. Everyone had a login and almost nobody opened it.

beats.trigger: **Name** the likely adoption failure before it happens, including the social failure that's hardest to see
beats.got: Five verbs, a list of outcomes. Only the failure one caught me.

beats.trigger: Two questions to warm up: who's the one person who came to mind just now? And what makes you hesitate about actually handing this to them?
beats.got: I thought of Mikko in pricing analytics. I hesitate because he would have to trust my context files, and they are only on my laptop.

beats.trigger: You are not going to ask *"what should I share with my teammate?"* That question is builder-centered
beats.got: Start from Mikko's job, not from what I built. This is a consultant's reflex I already have, but I usually skip it when I'm excited about my own tool.

beats.trigger: The test is specificity: does it name one teammate, their current way of doing the job, and an outcome you could observe?
beats.got: The agent read my files and wrote a job for Mikko. It's a usable test for whether the thing is generic. I'd have caught the generic line without being told, but the check is useful.

beats.trigger: If the reason is merely *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: Four shapes. I picked sharing the context, because that is my actual gap, and the agent had to justify it against Mikko's outcome and not against our tooling.

beats.trigger: You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Now find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can actually absorb it, then draft both halves of the plan.
beats.got: Next is the plan, and the bottleneck comes first.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: The agent clustered the obstacles. The real one was not technical: nobody owns the shared context, so each copy drifts. That is the thing I hadn't seen in my own situation.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: My technical plan looked good and my people plan was mostly UNASSIGNED. It was uncomfortable, and it is accurate. This is the first time the course produced something I could take to my team.

beats.trigger: [Test the sharing plan](test-the-sharing-plan.md) checks the assumptions underneath these plans
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: Treat the plans as hypotheses, not as done.

beats.trigger: *what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?*
beats.got: Mikko would have to believe the briefs match what the CFO asks about. That is an assumption I can test on him in an afternoon.

beats.trigger: The agent carries the strongest failure pressure into `module-7/monday.md`: one person, one question about how they do the job today, and one selected assumption with its test.
beats.got: Monday is one conversation with Mikko and one test. That is small enough to actually happen. One failure story, that he politely nods and goes back to his spreadsheet, was too close to home.

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping. A candidate picked because it moves the outcome is design.
beats.got: The whole exercise sequence in one paragraph. It is a good summary, though I had already got most of it.

beats.trigger: Industry analysts expect agent adoption to accelerate significantly over the coming years, which makes change management all the more important.
beats.got: nothing new. This is a generic change-management line that any consultancy deck would carry, and it has no connection to what I just built.

beats.trigger: The interview earned its keep when it found a third outcome past speed and quality: a dependency removed, an anxiety gone, a scope widened.
beats.got: Mostly a replay of the exercise, though the third-outcome idea is worth checking in my own Mikko file.

beats.trigger: Hand someone the agent file and you have handed them the shell of a thing whose contents are still on your disk and in your head.
beats.got: The agent file is the shell, and the value sits in my curated memory and corrections. That explains why my earlier forwarded prompts did nothing for anyone.

beats.trigger: Michael Polanyi, a philosopher of science, had the line for it: *we know more than we can tell.*
beats.got: People pick up what resembles work they already do. True, but a philosopher quote is not what I need on Tuesday.

beats.trigger: Remember that adoption is everyone's responsibility. Clear communication, strong sponsorship and regular follow-up remain the foundation, and agents are simply one more area where those principles apply.
beats.got: nothing new. It's a boilerplate sentence, and it cancels the sharper point right before it that the interface is the first piece with another person on the other side.

beats.trigger: The thing you would most like to hand over is the one thing that will not go.
beats.got: What I learned getting here can't be handed over, only the four artefacts. It's true and a bit humbling, but it is the same point as the big idea, made a second time.

beats.trigger: The before-and-after quote is how you know the sharpening reached the file, not just the summary.
beats.got: The debrief edits my sharing artefact in place and shows the actual changed lines. I like that I can verify it, and that I can push back and have it edit only the section I name.

beats.trigger: The artifact: the sharpened sharing file itself, plus one line in your Module 7 next-step file naming the first move.
beats.got: Leave with one sharpened file and one named next step.

beats.trigger: Access is easy; absorption is scarce.
beats.got: nothing new. A summary of what I already did.

beats.trigger: Come to Module 8 without one tested assumption or named person and you'll be reconstructing the contact while the opening exercise is already using the evidence. Your call.
beats.got: Run monday.md before the next module, or I fall behind. The deadline is clear and the tone isn't preachy, which I appreciated.

beats.trigger: What comes back from that contact is Module 8's raw material.
beats.got: nothing new

take_homes: Pick the person and their job first. Mikko's job, not my tool, decides what I share.
I can share context, a skill, the output or an interface. I can't share the agent. For my team the first shape is shared context, and it needs a named owner.
A people plan full of UNASSIGNED is the real finding. Fixing that comes before any more building.

monday.move: Ask Mikko how he builds the pricing-pilot brief today, then test one assumption: whether my brief matches the questions the CFO asks.
monday.when: Monday morning, in a 30-minute slot before the pricing working group
monday.stop_condition: If Mikko says he would not use the brief even if it were right, I stop and rework the job statement before building anything else.
monday.blocker: There is no shared location for the context files, and nobody is assigned to own them. I need to ask Jonas in IT for a shared folder or repo before I can hand Mikko anything.

misconception.why: I came in thinking better prompts were the skill. The module showed that what makes my output good is the curated context and the corrections, and that this is what my team lacks. I still think prompt quality matters, but it is no longer the main thing.

one_line: The exercises were useful and showed me my people plan was empty. The lecture is mostly a recap with a few boilerplate change-management lines that could go.
